name: Disk Full From Runaway Debug Logs
description: A junior dev pushed a config that switched the order service to log_level=DEBUG. Twelve hours later /var/log on mysql-srv-04 is 100% full, the binlog can't be written, the database goes read-only, and the app fleet starts rejecting writes.
reasoning: Two stateless app instances write to a single MySQL host that also acts as the central rsyslog target. The log volume from DEBUG mode hits MySQL's data partition because of a legacy mount layout and starves the binlog writer.

nodes.label: haproxy-edge-01
nodes.notes: Yes it's labelled nginx, it's actually HAProxy. Nobody renamed it in 2019.

nodes.label: mysql-srv-04
nodes.notes: MySQL 5.7 on RHEL 7. /var/log shares the same volume as binlogs.

narrative.text: Day-shift baseline. mysql-srv-04 / partition is sitting at 71%.
Disk usage crosses 90% — a Nagios warning fires but nobody acks.
Disk hits 100%. MySQL flips to read-only ('Can't create/write to file: No space left on device').
Order writes start failing. App-srv-07 returns 500s on POST /orders.
Engineer rotates and gzips old debug logs; gains 14% headroom.
DEBUG logging reverted to INFO via Salt. MySQL exits read-only.
Backlog of failed orders re-queued; latency still elevated as queue drains.
All green. PM tracks a follow-up to split log volume from data volume.
